questions.q: In bird population of newly formed volcanic island, a rare allele of a gene was noted to be much more prevalent than the populations of same species on the mainland. This is known as ______ effect.
questions.solution:
In bird population of newly formed volcanic island, a rare allele of a gene was noted to be much more prevalent than the populations of same species on the mainland. This is known as founder effect.

Explanation:

Founder Effect occurs when a small group of individuals colonizes a new area (like a volcanic island), leading to a higher frequency of certain rare alleles due to limited genetic variation. This results in genetic differences compared to the original mainland population.

questions.q:
What is reproductive isolation?



Name any three types of premating isolating mechanisms.



Name any three types of postmating isolating mechanisms.
questions.solution:
Reproductive isolation occurs due to changes in genetic material, gene pool, and structure of genital organs. It prevents interbreeding between populations.


Pre-mating or pre-zygotic isolating mechanism: This mechanism prevents fertilization and zygote formation.

  1. Habitat isolation or (Ecological isolation): Members of a population living in the same geographic region but occupying separate habitats in such a way that potential mates do not meet.
  2. Seasonal or temporal isolation: Members of a population living in the same geographic region but are sexually mature at different years or different times of the year.
  3. Ethological isolation: Due to specific mating behavior the members of the population do not mate.
  4. Mechanical Isolation: Members of two populations have differences in the structure of reproductive organs.


  1. Gamete mortality: Gametes have a limited life span. Due to one or the other reasons, if the union of the two gametes does not occur in the given time, it results in gamete mortality.
  2. Zygote mortality: Here, the egg is fertilized but the zygote dies due to one or the other reasons.
  3. Hybrid sterility: Hybrids develop to maturity but become sterile due to failure of proper gametogenesis (meiosis). e.g., Mule is an intergeneric hybrid that is sterile.

questions.q:
Explain vestigeal organs as evidence of evolution.



Give any two examples of vestigeal organs in human beings.
questions.solution:
Vestigial organs are reduced or non-functional structures in an organism that were functional in their ancestors. They provide evidence for evolution by showing that species have changed over time, losing traits that are no longer needed. Examples include the human appendix, whale hind limb bones, and flightless bird wings, which indicate common ancestry and evolutionary adaptation.



  • Appendix: A small pouch attached to the large intestine, which was once used for digesting cellulose in ancestral herbivores but has lost its main function in humans.
  • Coccyx (Tailbone): The remnant of a tail from primate ancestors, now serving as an attachment point for muscles but no longer used for balance or movement.

questions.q: Explain natural selection with the example of industrial melanism.
questions.solution:
Industrial melanism is one of the best examples of natural selection.

In Great Britain, before industrialization (1845) grey white winged moths (Biston betularia) were more in number than black-winged moth (Biston carbonaria).

These moths are nocturnal and during day time they rest on a tree trunks. The white winged moth can camouflaged (hide in the background) well with the lichen-covered trees that helped them to escape from the predatory birds.

On other hand, the black-winged moth resting on lichen covered tree trunks were easy victims for the predatory birds and their number was reduced. During industrial revolution, large number of industries came up in Great Britain. The industries released black sooty smoke that covered and killed the lichens growing on trees and turn the tree black due to pollution. This change become an advantage to the black-winged moth that camouflaged well with the black tree trunks and their number increased while the white-winged moth become victim to predatory birds due to which their number reduced. Thus natural selection has resulted in the establishment of phenotypic traits in changing the environmental conditions.

questions.q: Define ‘reproductive isolation’ and explain two types of reproductive isolation.
questions.solution:
Reproductive Isolation: Prevents interbreeding between the populations whether they are geographically isolation or living close together.
Types of Isolating mechanisms :
1. Pre -mating or pre-zygotic isolating mechanisms : In habitat Isolation, members of a population living in the same region occupy different habitat. Thus potential mates do not meet. In seasonal isolation, members of a population attains sexual isolation, members of a population attain sexual maturity at the different times, thus preventing interbreeding.
In ethological isolation, members of two populations have different mating behaviours. This prevents interbreeding.
In mechanical isolation, the members of two populations have differences in the structure of reproductive organs. So interbreeding is not possible.
2. Post-matting or post zygotic isolating mechanisms are : Gamete mortality (Sperms transfer takes place but egg is not fertilized), Zygote mortality (Egg is fertilized but zygote dies) and hybrid sterility (Hybrids are sterile)

questions.q:
Define organic evolution.



Give the principles of Darwin's theory of natural selection.



Objection to Darwin's theory of natural selection.
questions.solution:
Organic evolution is a slow, gradual, continuous and irreversible change through which the present-day complex forms have descended from their simple pre-existing forms of the past.



Principles of Darwinism:
Darwin’s theory of organic evolution by natural selection is based on the following principles:

  1. Over production or prodigality of production:
    All organisms have a natural tendency to over produce.
    If this tendency is not checked, then even a single species of a plant or animal will occupy
    the entire space available on the earth. 
  2.  Struggle for existence: Organisms multiply in geometric ratio, but space and food remain
    constant leading to competition for survival. Increase in the number of species leads to a
    competition called struggle for existence
  3. Variations and Heredity:The differences which occur between the closely related organisms are called variations.It is universal law of nature. Variations may be favourable or unfavourable.
  4. Survival of the fittest or natural selection:According to Darwin, in the struggle for existence, the fittest individuals survive andreproduce, while the unfit individuals perish. 
  5. Origin of new species:According Darwin, useful variations appear in every generation and are inherited from one generation to another.


  1. Natural selection is not the only factor responsible for evolution
  2. Darwin did not mention any explanation about useful and useless modifications
  3. There is no explanation about slow changes and abrupt changes.
